scientific_hypothesis: Placing the lower-index SiO2 layer adjacent to air and the higher-index TiO2 layer adjacent to the glass substrate will yield a local minimum in mean reflectance, potentially satisfying the soft target of <0.03 if the thicknesses are tuned to create destructive interference across the 450-700 nm band.
expected_advantages: Deterministic grid search eliminates optimizer stochastic failure modes
Explicit 2-layer topology resolves the previous compilation mismatch
SiO2-first ordering provides a smoother index transition from air
known_risks: The discrete material indices (1.46, 2.40) may not perfectly match the ideal theoretical indices for a two-layer AR on glass (n=1.52), limiting the minimum achievable reflectance
Thickness bounds (40-160 nm) may exclude the optimal quarter-wave thicknesses for certain wavelengths in the band
expected_observations: best_target_score should converge to a value representing the inverse of the minimum achievable mean reflectance for this specific topology
valid_candidates should equal 1 if the optimizer finds a solution within bounds, or 0 if the constraint set is infeasible (unlikely given bounds)
If the hypothesis holds, the resulting mean reflectance should be significantly lower than a single-layer equivalent, potentially approaching but not necessarily below 0.03
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improvement relative to the previous iteration in the internal loop is < 1e-4 for 3 consecutive steps, judge local convergence reached -> stop refinement and return current best
If valid_candidates = 0, judge that no solution exists within the 40-160 nm bounds for this topology -> terminate route and flag constraint infeasibility
